notes.title: Task Force 0.7.0.2124
notes.notes:
[b]This is probably one of the most important updates we've ever made.[/b] Not to be too overdramatic or emotional, but having an automated ladder system was the entire dream of this game from the get-go. You see, this game started off as a mod on Insurgency called Resurgence. It was a total conversion mod for Insurgency that created an entire 3rd person mode along with a robust server infrastructure that offered stats, rankings, and a custom clan ladder. We had our own website where players could register their clans, send/accept challenges, and schedule ladder matches.

These players would then join any set of "war servers" where they could type "!ready" in the chat, and if the remote website could find a scheduled match, it would reserve the "war server" for that match, almost like going to a basketball court in a public park and starting up a game. It would download the entire roster list, prevent any players that weren't on the rosters from joining the server, and automate the entire match process. You couldn't switch teams, the maps were already preset, and everything just ran according to the rules of the ladder.

However, this system was very limiting because it required a set of pre-allocated servers to basically just "sit around" waiting for people to claim them. It wasn't scalable, and couldn't be rolled out on a mass scale. But it was literally at this exact moment that we saw the future of what we were trying to create. It was essentially the complete merger of both SOCOM and GameBattles, where clans could play ladder matches without the need to have the losing team "report the loss" or require a staff of admins/referees just to deal with all that bullshit.

And it is today that we finally have the modern re-creation of this system, one that we pioneered over 9 years ago on Resurgence, fully working and integrated into OUR OWN GAME BUILT FROM SCRATCH...Task Force! So without further ado, we present to you, the Task Force Competitive Ladder System!!!


We've setup an entirely temporary system that allows complete access to the ladder via a Discord Bot. That means you can access the ladder even while on-the-go from anywhere, using the Discord mobile app. This system will eventually be integrated into the game itself, with custom menus, ect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/7471ad5286e4fdf91e29331a33babf121698982e.gif[/img]

You start by registering a team using the `/register` command in the chat. You can create any type of team you wish, whether it's an entire clan, squads team, doubles team, or singles profile. If you're registering a clan, you can reserve a clan tag on the ladder that NO OTHER TEAM CAN USE. It will be unique to your clan, and only members of your clan will have this tag.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/6da9c81de384c1e7cb62cab61c63f4738b16968d.gif[/img]

You can then send roster invites to other players in the game using their Steam IDs:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/a227e113953e2a6069dcd21a0a5978b592b91312.gif[/img]

You can use the `/roster list` command to view your roster for a specific ladder type:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/7919d0d164e722b38324325547240295ee2c9e78.gif[/img]

You can also promote members to "admins" so that they can send/accept challenges and schedule matches for your team, since basic members do not have the ability to manage your clan (and can only play in scheduled matches). Most importantly, to reduce the abuse of "ringers" you must register a player 12 hours in advance prior to a match for them to be on the roster for that match.

You can view the current stats/ranking of your team using the `/team profile` command:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/9dd46a8909bb144893a40f13923c8b6c0bdbd250.gif[/img]

Once you post on the match finder and organize a scheduled match with another team, you can send them a "challenge" using the `/challenge send` command:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/05b11484fb00800e1baf1fc4ac14015a62c3df42.gif[/img]

The opposing team can then "accept" this challenge using the `/challenge accept` command:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/4b0c4e19c2f0f2d61e3668e16d7bd066c1adb0bc.gif[/img]

Once a challenge is accepted, an official match will be scheduled on the ladder. You can check the upcoming matches for your team using the `/match schedule` command:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/7a8d0dd813198732adfd36f20f22cfc979e5f55e.gif[/img]

Now that a match is scheduled, here is where the real magic happens! When it's close to the time for your match, our entirely AUTOMATED SERVER INFRASTRUCTURE will just create a server for your match, INSTANTLY! We've setup an entire geo-location service that calculates the optimal location for the server, based on the location of all the players on each roster:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/49808753a9993d2df65f8415ac4c4f484695ee95.png[/img]

It will automatically cross-reference this information with your entire team along with the entire opposing team in order to select the most optimal server location for everyone in the match:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/c59e6bf8b883260e6f9bb39c873c1bd1abef7059.png[/img]

You just boot up the game right before your match is scheduled to start, and you'll see a server for your teams. Nobody else can join this server, it's completely restricted to only the authorized players on each rosters, so no password or anything is required to join:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/4bac69148676681fb04d2d31032216562815d43e.png[/img]

Once in the match server you'll be in a temporary "respawn lobby" where everyone is waiting for the match to start. You can go to the "players" screen to see a bunch of "green up" icons, where each player has to "green up" in order to start the match. After every player in the game is ready, the match will start:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/801f1ad927b12a7bc361c1244441f8467c7effd5.png[/img]

Then you just play out the entire match, without worrying about anything! After the match is over, all the stats data will be logged for the match, including the final outcome of which teams won/lost. The losing team DOES NOT need to head over to the website to "report the loss" it just does everything automatically:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/f7751dc041d010c2880f3c9a35d3e01848918bdb.png[/img]

Once the match is over, the server will be automatically destroyed after 5 minutes, so that more servers can be created for upcoming matches. And that's it! The process is really that simple, it's an entirely AUTOMATED LADDER SYSTEM!!! Just the way we dreamed of it many years ago, now finally ready for testing! If you want to get in early and help test the new ladder system, be sure to join the official Task Force Discord for more information: discord.gg/zGha2gtFzX

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.7.2078
notes.notes:
This update includes a temporary workaround for a critical issue with accelerated paint that would cause some players with both dedicated and integrated graphics (usually laptops) to experience a "black screen" when booting the game. You would still hear the main menu music in the background shortly after the opening logo animation, but the entire game screen would remain black.

We now have a workaround in place that detects when accelerated paint isn't working and will show a temporary popup to reinitialize the user interface with accelerated paint disabled. This means users experiencing this issue can now play the game without needing to create any kind of annoying desktop shortcut. We still plan to actually fix this problem in a future update, but for now at least players have a way to get around the issue without having to troubleshoot anything.

The update also addresses a few performance-related issues that were encountered in the previous update. We rolled back a few important changes and then slowly re-implemented them with our testing group to figure out what was causing the problem, and now performance should be back to normal.

There's a new TaskForceLight blueprint interface that we've added to workshop projects as well. This allows workshop mappers to setup environments with lights that will automatically turn on and off based on the "time of day" when using the built-in sky system that comes with the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/5119544078dd0dbb47679777976c042140ce8321.gif[/img]

Finally there's an all new update system integrated into our custom workshop launcher. You can now update your workshop projects with the click of a button, rather than needing to create a new project entirely and move your files over.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/411aaa58de7ba1613ce6156eb3632cad04fc1c47.png[/img]

This makes updating workshop projects a lot easier than before, and everything is carefully outlined in the documentation on GitHub:

[url=https://github.com/tracerinteractive/TaskForce#update-project]https://github.com/tracerinteractive/TaskForce#update-project[/url]

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.6.2069
notes.notes:
This update makes some very significant optimizations across various systems. The character rotation system, which sends quite a lot of data, has now been optimized so it no longer floods the network (as it was the first thing to start dropping in low bandwidth scenarios). The audio systems for bullet impacts and footstep sounds have also been optimized. This means footstep sounds or impact sounds will be completely ignored when they aren't within a certain radius of your point-of-view. The automatic level bounds system has been updated as well to include the "relevant to level bounds" option within the engine, which provides workshop mappers with more control over determining the bottom of the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/4c3577d63571bcb13614642a899e69f52e0f05d8.gif[/img]

The "audio glitch" has been fixed! We've completely removed "bink audio" so it can no longer cause us any problems. Previously if you played for a certain amount of time (or a lot of audio data was being loaded) it would cause your weapon sounds to no longer play. This means you would hear bullets impacting around you, but even though you saw your weapon firing it wouldn't make any sounds. It also was the primary reason your game would crash. This issue even required a full restart of the game in order to fix and happened quite frequently. So having it corrected is a major step forward towards being ready to put the buy button back up on the store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/ce88346a854524bc8944604f4d477fca3a4dd6b2.jpg[/img]

We've made a very significant optimization pass on our petrochemical plant map. It should now get a much higher FPS than before as we're now properly instancing many of the modular meshes used throughout the map. There's also an initial optimization pass performed on our military outpost map since the landscape and road meshes were causing extreme FPS drops and preventing the map from being tested.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/8bcf2fa212d1d0ccb77da53a4220f2e0cdd6a6b9.jpg[/img]

The climbing system has been updated so you can now press your action button to "pull up" when hanging on a ledge. Previously you would have to either move forwards or backwards to either "pull up" or "drop down" but this wasn't very intuitive for new players. So now when hanging the climb system will display another popup that says "press to climb" for those that are unaware of the existing gameplay mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/281037bab076f364fa9b6f63bb152eb99773fecb.jpg[/img]

An issue where death replication wouldn't trigger has now been corrected. This would occasionally cause players to go into T-pose rather than ragdoll after dying. It was due to some network replication delays but should no longer be an issue. Another bug was also corrected that would cause your weapon trigger to get stuck when spamming buttons. This should no longer happen since the weapon system doesn't have the ability to artificially delay shots anymore.

Finally the workshop system has been updated so you can setup custom "player skins" without actually including any skins at all. This means you can customize the audio queues of the existing character skins that come with the game. Therefore workshop mappers can now include custom grenade callouts and dynamic voice taunts as well. However keep in mind that using voice taunts before the round is over will give away your position on the map.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.5.2041
notes.notes:
This update includes a ton of new Unreal Engine 5 assets that we're testing. Here's an example of a new map we're planning for a military outpost:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/a0a6c30e51132dbb1c9568944803a027d06cd72c.jpg[/img]

There's also dynamic weather that we've setup so the map is sometimes day time or night time, which will automatically enable/disable dynamic lighting such as industrial lights and spotlights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/449f2141bc1723521b075784f404ecdca7dc6b42.jpg[/img]

We plan to add a lot more assets over the coming weeks as well. This should make the game feel fresh and up-to-date prior to re-releasing back on the store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/f60894e0368440f83e10ddccf7c9848f00917083.jpg[/img]

This update also addresses a critical issue with throwables falling through the ground when landing in water. It fixes a problem with footsteps as well that caused them to sound as if they're behind the player when spectating another player.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.4.2037
notes.notes:
This update fixes a critical bug with water volumes interacting with bullets and the new lean mechanic. If a player was leaning in water it would cause them to "go sliding" due to the lean pushaway system hitting all the water. It was also not possible to shoot through water using the current bullet mechanics. We've now corrected these issues and leaning in water should no longer be a problem and bullets should currently ignore water completely until we implement proper penetration mechanics and particle effects for this special case scenario.

The update also includes water noises when the player is moving through deep water. These sounds will scale based on the depth of the water and trigger whenever you're moving or turning in water.

Finally this update addresses an important issue with footsteps sounding as if they're behind the player. We've corrected the problem and the new footstep audio system should properly keep these sounds in front of the camera for the currently visible player.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.3.2034
notes.notes:
This update fixes a critical issue with water replication. There were some inconsistencies with the networking between servers and clients with these new movement mechanics, so now these issues have been addressed. We've also utilized the integrated water system that comes with the engine for determining water depth which means custom water volumes are no longer required since everything just automatically works now.

We've addressed another issue with workshop maps that prevented certain engine assets from loading due to the content not being part of the game. Now workshop mappers should be able to utilize all types of water assets without having any broken materials after cooking and uploading your map.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.2.2028
notes.notes:
This update overhauls all the animations for the new leaning system. The character will now keep their feet more planted and actually moves the weapon to the left when leaning to the left. So now your "other right" (left) can finally shoot around corners too!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/de863b7a326050b5116a58fb21b9304cbd31bdd9.gif[/img]

Please note this is a slowed down view of the animation. [i]We also have an all new ADS system coming in a future update with new FPS arms along with sights, scopes, and snipers. So until then the animation only needs to support hip fire for the time being.[/i]

The update includes all new water mechanics as well. There are now "water volumes" available which slow down player movement based on the water depth. If the water is not shallow enough then you will be prevented from proning. The same goes for crouching where you cannot crouch in water that's deep enough to put your weapon underwater. In both these situations the movement system will automatically force the character to stand up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/6cc7b46827ca7e9dcadbbf7e6bec434b9cbea5d1.gif[/img]

If you find yourself in water that is so deep you cannot even stand in it without your weapon being underwater, then you will be killed with a "has drowned" killfeed message. So don't tread out too far!

This should prevent players from abusing water areas on various maps. The footsteps system has been updated as well so that you make proper splashing sounds when moving through shallow water. However we haven't setup any special effects for deep water scenarios just yet, such as ripples and whooshing noises.

We've setup buoyancy for ragdolls too!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/6844fdfc05c018209fb85be52df172d45fd1da4b.gif[/img]

There's also a new water blueprint that's available for workshop mappers to designate which areas of their map consist of water. In a future update we'll include more buoyancy support for other physics-based objects as well.

Finally the update addresses an issue with footsteps not registering when running downhill on certain types of objects. Now these sounds should register a bit more often, but there's still some testing and fine tuning required for things such as staircases.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.1.2015
notes.notes:
This update includes a ton of new Unreal Engine 5 assets that we're testing. Here's an example of a new map we're planning for a petrochemical plant:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/7d3e4c8016bcb9906fac0592e81fa479c72ee792.jpg[/img]

There's also dynamic weather that we've setup so the map is sometimes party cloudy, raining, or even an all out thunderstorm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/20abb79b4ad5a5b9696460fb6c104dcd8971447e.jpg[/img]

We plan to add a lot more assets over the coming weeks as well. This should make the game feel fresh and up-to-date prior to re-releasing back on the store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/e8f8ed3ae8183a31f5c1a127ecce96383aa73ba7.jpg[/img]

The update also makes some critical changes to explosive forces, which will apply most specifically to grenade damage priorities. The previous system would just randomly loop through each player on the map and didn't provide any concrete output in terms of the order that players were killed.

Now explosive forces will apply any and all damage to each hostage or VIP inside the damage radius before applying damage to each individual player based on their distance. This means an explosion will damage the closest player and then work outwards applying damage as a real explosion would. However this also prevents players from abusing the mechanic by killing a player first even though that explosion would have actually killed the hostages or VIPs as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/1494cb26cd390e4529340b75cbcbf34a866ea6d9.gif[/img]

The update implements a new system for console messages that allows dedicated servers to redirect output to clients. This is very important to admin commands as there was previously no information being provided when a command was submitted, which made it quite difficult to know why a command wasn't actually working.

We've added an automatic AFK kicking system that monitors whether or not players are actually playing each round. If a player is AFK for a certain period of time the server will kick this player while still allowing them to rejoin, whereas the admin kick command would prevent the player from rejoining for a certain period of time. There's also a custom disconnect message that says that player was "kicked for being AFK" rather than "disconnected" so other players can know when someone was kicked automatically rather than by an admin.

There's now a physics restriction on weapons when dropping them to the ground which limits the speed at which they can move. This should prevent weapons from flying very far or unrealistically whereas they should now fall to the ground more appropriately. We've also added some important debug output for the new user interface system as more DirectX 12 functionality is built out behind the scenes until we make the switch back from DirectX 11 later this year.

notes.title: Task Force 0.6.0.2001
notes.notes:
This update changes the default renderer from DirectX 12 to DirectX 11. We're making this change because after extensive testing we've determined that the game runs smoother this way without really losing too many new UE5 features that we don't necessarily need right now. That's because we value performance much more than graphics, even though we want to make a game that still has good graphics. So until we update from UE5.2 to UE5.4 later this year for some extensive performance updates to DirectX 12 in UE5, we plan to keep everything defaulted to DirectX 11 until then.

If you would like to test the game on DirectX 12 then you can use a special command line parameter via a desktop shortcut in order to launch the game in this graphics mode:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/79ba723c287512f59b577584fc4a280b283b8e0b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/e5ed42c6bc41856d5bd16ed383fbdf5f451af376.png[/img]

There are still some significant benefits to DirectX 12 along with many optimizations that save developers time so they don't have to optimize their assets as much. So by falling back to DirectX 11 you do lose some of these newer benefits, and it's worth trying out which mode works best for your current system. But again based on all of our tester feedback it appears that DirectX 11 was the preferred renderer a majority of the time, with players noticing very little change in how good the graphics actually looked.

This update also overhauls the entire audio system with some very significant optimizations and reorganizations. We've setup audio priorities for every single audio sample in the game so the engine can know which sounds are most important in order to prioritize them over others to ensure they always play. This is because audio engines are limited by a certain number of channels that they can mix together before the engine has to start choosing which sounds to play and which sounds to drop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/166bfeb834145d13352615da8b28a56ffb49fb0e.gif[/img]

The weapon optimizations are very significant as we're no long spamming the game world with audio and particle components to simulate weapon fire. Instead we now have a much more robust system that properly cycles through preallocated audio and particle effects that repeat in order to simulate the effect of constant firing. This should make the shooting feel a bit snappier as the entire system is now using a lot less resources. We've also added new "dry fire" sounds to the weapons which should trigger when you try to fire the weapon when it's out of ammo.

We've included accelerated paint support for DirectX 12 now as well. This means the DirectX 12 user interface will be just as snappy and quick as the DirectX 11 user interface after our previous update last week. This means accelerated paint mode is being officially rolled out across both rendering platforms and ensures that your web-based user interface (a web browser floating on top of the game engine) works at full 4K 60FPS. That's because the underlying system is now sharing a live texture from the web browser with the game engine, which allows for instant graphics copying rather than the extremely slow process that previously had to go through the CPU. Now that everything stays on the GPU the entire user interface system is extremely quick and snappy compared to before, and will work just as fluidly at 4K resolutions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/9a8ac32571b6ceca58c498eb261488bc397cf060.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/298e8b1adce2e85a522adbd196c84e326565f429.gif[/img]

This also means we've removed the temporary 90 FPS cap in the game, which was in place to prevent the game engine from overloading the web browser and causing the entire user interface to lock up. Now with accelerated paint we no longer have to worry about the game engine and the web browser fighting for CPU power, and you can run your entire game now with a completely uncapped FPS if you'd like.

We fixed a critical issue with workshop blueprints breaking between map changes. This caused doors and other workshop components to glitch out and have multiple copies on the map, because the "fake" ones that are used in-editor to place around were accidentally showing up in-game when they shouldn't. This also made it difficult to pick up the bomb at times as it would appear that there were two different bombs on the ground. The grenade arc has been fixed up as well and should now no longer appear overly dark or create any kind of "glowing" effect in the game world. We've also disabled all post processes on workshop maps which should prevent custom maps from using undesired features such as motion blur, film grain, vignettes, auto exposure, and more.

This update makes some very significant performance optimizations for Steam Deck. We've completely reconfigured the entire graphics system in UE5 for Steam Deck with automatic detection of the platform and implementing default settings that provide a smooth gameplay experience on Steam Deck. There's even special graphics modes that we're using to provide the best performance possible which would normally not be necessary on PC, so hopefully these updates really help to provide the best experience possible on Steam Deck.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/973b801a4ffda3f0289257e7ebdab79e1424e351.png[/img]

A small issue in the training map was corrected where you'd keep your weapon from the previous round. This should no longer be the case in the training map anymore. Another bug was also addressed regarding the HUD completely freezing. This was not because of any user interface issues, but because of a certain data connection breaking between the server and your game client. However there's still some extensive testing required for us to confirm this issue is indeed fixed, as there might be more to it depending on how testing goes.

The "map" command has been fixed so that it will now look for existing maps in the maplist prior to loading the requested map. This allows the command to maintain the existing round timer and total rounds from the maplist rather than using the default 3 rounds as was previously happening. It's also very smart in that if a map appears on the maplist multiple times but with different game modes, it will actually pick the proper settings from the maplist that match the desired game mode rather than picking the first match in the maplist.

Finally this update overhauls the entire collision and physics of the third-person camera. We've added an entire "smooth gliding" system that prevents the camera from stuttering or glitching out for quick instants, which especially happens when running through doors or underneath other objects. Now the camera will pop forward but slowly slide outwards to create a very subtle effect that allows the player to focus more on their aiming and less on their camera collision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/91a59db7318ff83ec620817bee54b528f51e4a01.gif[/img]

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.16.1986
notes.notes:
This update makes some significant performance enhancements to the user interface system. We are now using something called "accelerated paint" in order to provide a much more responsive and snappier UI. However this system is currently only in place for DirectX 11 and is not finalized on DirectX 12, which means you would have to manually switch into this graphics mode for the time being. However this is a huge step forward for us to ensure we have a user interface that runs smoothly at a similar FPS to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/79ba723c287512f59b577584fc4a280b283b8e0b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/92eed0efe1fd0f6e211e42991011f69fc24907c9.png[/img]

There's also been some adjustments to smoke grenades, which should now deploy faster than before, as the timer has been reduced by 1 second. We've added some new graphics commands as well to disable some newer features such as virtual shadow maps via the graphics_vsm command.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.15.1980
notes.notes:
This update adjusts a lot of settings for Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections. We've carefully tuned some default engine settings which should fix a lot of issues with existing maps and things being a bit too dark. There is now a significant amount of indoor lighting to prevent things from over-darkening along with some boosting to texture colors.

There's also an important fix for auto-exposure settings which weren't originally tuned very well for a competitive shooter. These settings are what adjust the exposure of your eyes as you walk into light areas vs dark areas. We've now overridden the entire auto-exposure system in the engine so that it performs as intended. The same goes for workshop maps which should inherit all of these settings by default.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.14.1979
notes.notes:
This update enables Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections by default. It includes some optimized settings to ensure these new lighting modes run as efficiently as possible. These new features are what make everything "pop" in Unreal Engine 5, but (as we always do) we wanted to focus on performance fixes prior to experimenting with these new rendering features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/07fce1e8a5e1b1c261823df298460eef07a4b891.gif[/img]

As you can see, these new GI and reflection modes significantly increase the graphical fidelity of the game. There are now actual light bounces that adjust the color of surfaces to create a much more sophisticated representation of a scene. It also creates high quality reflections that can now show elements that are completely off-screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/0a79091ee16da02d21e2cf87d42cc9e420e69e52.gif[/img]

However while these new lighting modes look fantastic, we want to ensure performance is never compromised. Therefore we've included some new graphics settings that allow players to manually enable/disable these new features if they aren't desired. The following commands can be used to control Lumen settings:

[list][*]graphics_lumen[*]graphics_lumen_gi[*]graphics_lumen_reflections[/list]

These settings will save with your other video settings for the local device and are not synchronized via Steam Cloud as is the case with bindings, gameplay settings, ect.

In the workshop editor, a post process system can also forcibly disable Lumen on workshop maps if modders don't want these lighting features available on their maps at all. Finally we've included an engine system that detects if Lumen is disabled and automatically forces skylights to be stationary, otherwise they would have significant shadow artifacts without Lumen enabled.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.13.1974
notes.notes:
This update fixes an important issue with server disconnect messages. There are lots of custom systems running for our workshop integration which provide automatic downloading of maps on the loading screen, map version checking, automatic map updates, ect. But if a server is out of date and has an older version of a workshop map, this will prevent players from joining that server when they have a newer version of the map.

However these types of disconnects from the loading screen were not supported with our UI error messages. The only way players knew about these issues was if they checked the console to see what errors were being output. So we've addressed this issue and fully integrated the loading screen systems with our UI error messages to prevent confusion when joining servers with custom content.

The update also includes all new "graphics" commands that let players adjust the quality settings of the engine. There are 3 different levels of quality (low, medium, and high) for the following graphical settings:

[list][*]View Distance[*]Anti-Aliasing[*]Shadows[*]Global Illumination[*]Reflections[*]Post-Process[*]Textures[*]Visual Effects[*]Foliage[*]Shading[/list]

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.12.1970
notes.notes:
This update fixes an issue where weapons would not reset when selecting a new weapon if picking up an enemy weapon. The new carry-over feature between rounds would prevent weapon selection until death and selecting a new weapon would not overwrite this feature. So this has been addressed to prevent future conflicts between selecting weapons vs picking up enemy weapons.

There's also some important debugging information that we've setup to allow us to fix a critical issue with the HUD freezing between map changes. This causes the timer, player diamonds, ping graph, scoreboard, and other elements to stop working between map changes and is one of the next major bugs we'd like to get fixed. So this is an important step into addressing this issue.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.11.1968
notes.notes:
This update fixes a critical performance issue with the new UE5 ragdolls. There should no longer be any stutter when players die whereby ragdolls fall to the ground. We've also significantly optimized when players spawn into the game, which should reduce any network spikes or stutters that take place between round resets.

There's a new weapon carry-over system that's been implemented between rounds. Now if you pick up an enemy weapon and stay alive until the end of the round, you'll keep that enemy weapon into the next round and continue to have this weapon until you either die or the map is over. We're also detecting if players haven't left the spawn yet, which allows you to change your weapon without waiting until the next round. Note that you can only change your weapon once per round and must not have moved from the spot where you spawned on the map.

Another critical issue has been addressed that prevented players from receiving credit for kills from grenades, breach points, or C-4 if the player had already died. Therefore you should now be properly credited with a kill and the associated points if your grenade kills an enemy after you die.

We've updated our anti-cheat system with some of the latest definitions, but we're not going to elaborate on this for obvious reasons. Finally some crashes have been fixed relating to when players fall out of the map or when weapons are being cleaned up by the server.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.10.1950
notes.notes:
This update makes some very important changes to the new stats and rankings system. Previously if a player left the game before it was over there was no "game over" calculations on that account when the server sends final stats after the final round. This means you could leave in the middle of a game and neither receive a loss nor a win since you weren't there for the end of the game. However for a competitive system to function correctly we need to penalize players that try to leave "competitive mode" early before the game is over. Therefore we now find all players from the stats history of the current game that are no longer connected to the server and put a game loss on their account for leaving early.

We plan to add a popup message in the next update when quitting the match early if the server is in "competitive mode" along with a "competitive timeout" so players are aware of this penalty when trying to quit back to the main menu. Note that a player can re-join a match before it is over to prevent receiving any penalty and complete the game as normal.

The update also fixes an issue with the bomb icon indicator when someone has picked up the bomb. This icon would not display on the player after the round was over as all the other diamonds do, which should now be corrected. Finally an issue has been addressed in the bullet tracing system that prevented the physics types of surfaces on dynamic meshes from being known on impact. This was causing "purple impacts" to display on certain physics-enabled objects such as weapons players drop of they die.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.9.1949
notes.notes:
This update adds new "slay" and "spec" commands for server admins. They can now force players to commit suicide when they're AFK without kicking them or even move them to the spectators instead. Be sure to use the "players" command to obtain a list of players in the server along with their associated Steam IDs.

The round stats screen should now display whether or not players died that round. We've temporarily slashed out any player that died until we implement some new icons for the round stats screen. An issue with certain weapons not having proper physics types has been corrected as well. You should no longer see purple bullet impacts on weapons dropped on the ground that you shoot.

Finally we've included the Landmass and Water plugins within the game along with all associated content. These plugins have also been enabled in the Task Force Editor, so mappers should update their engine installation along with any project configurations in order to get the latest settings. [i]Please note that this doesn't mean we've included built-in water mechanics that work with the game, but rather an initial water plugin that allows you to make more advanced water surfaces. We still have to program our own system for representing underwater volumes and how they affect your character depending on how deep they are in the water.[/i]

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.8.1945
notes.notes:
This update implements an initial user-interface to check player rankings. The interface is very basic for now since it will only be used for testing in order to verify ranks are being calculated correctly. [b]Please note that stats will be RESET multiple times over the coming weeks as we carefully test and tune everything before re-release.[/b] However we still need your help to collect stats now so we can ensure everything is working correctly ahead of time.

We've also setup titles and paygrades which should now display on the player stats screen. It will say E-1 through E-9 for enlisted and O-1 through O-7 for ranked officers. Finally, the number of rounds required to become ranked has been TEMPORARILY reduced as well to allow us to test things faster.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.7.1944
notes.notes:
This update enables the new stats and rankings system on dedicated servers and implements an initial user-interface to check your stats. The interface is very basic for now since it will only be used for testing in order to verify stats are being logged correctly. In the next update we plan to build out this interface into a very robust and detailed set of data and graphs, including stats for each individual weapon along with daily, weekly, and monthly stats. [b]Please note that stats will be RESET multiple times over the coming weeks as we carefully test and tune everything before re-release.[/b] However we still need your help to collect stats now so we can ensure everything is working correctly ahead of time.

The rank icons next to your name in the bottom-left (and on the round/game stats screens) are now LIVE. This means they are hooked up to the rankings system on the website and will refresh your current rank after every round. Please note that these icons are only visible in dedicated servers, but do not display in user-created lobbies or offline games. These rank icons are now also relayed to Discord so they can display in your Discord activity. This means you can click on someone's profile in Discord and see their LIVE rank next to the current server info, such as current map, mode, player count, ect.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.6.1942
notes.notes:
This update adds console commands for controller players to adjust sensitivity, deadzone, acceleration, and invert the controller. These commands start with controller_* and are similar to the commands for the mouse.

The FPS command has been tweaked so that it TEMPORARILY enforces a 90 FPS maximum, although it will still save your desired FPS for a future update. That means if you try to set your FPS to 144 it will still save as 144 but for now will load in as 90. We've implemented this TEMPORARILY in order to mitigate some issues we're experiencing with our UI system on Unreal Engine 5. It should prevent your user-interfaces such as the menu and HUD from becoming extremely laggy.

Finally we fixed an issue with global sound configurations in the engine that were not being set correctly. This means your menu volume on the main menu will now save when you close the game, as will your music volume as well.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.5.1938
notes.notes:
This update adds all new headshot indicators to the game. There will now be a headshot icon in the kill feed if a player was killed with a headshot, and headshot information will be displayed on the stats screen at the end of the round if a player had any headshot kills.

The game settings have also been expanded for various audio channels. This will allow you adjust the volume for different parts of the game. These settings will also save via Steam Cloud Sync so you can keep the same settings across any of your computers.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.4.1936
notes.notes:
This update makes some significant changes to the new jumping mechanics. There is now a bit of movement that takes place when jumping off the ground. It should allow players to jump onto ledges when standing up against them without interfering with the new jumping mechanics. It was very important that these adjustments provided a bit of forward momentum when jumping from a position where the player is standing in-place without causing the momentum of jumping while moving to feel somewhat askew because of these changes.

The MVP screen at the end of the game has now been fixed and should properly pick players for both teams. It will select the player with the highest score on each team, or if tied, will then select based on kills, assists, and damage done to the enemy team. Additionally the "music" command has been fixed and should properly save within your game settings which are synchronized via Steam Cloud (which means you maintain the same settings across all computers that are logged in with your Steam account).

A critical issue where character ragdolls wouldn't clean up between rounds if the player left the game before the round is over has been addressed. This was a very serious issue that caused all kinds of "frozen bodies" in A-pose to be visible throughout random parts of a map (since these ragdolls were never cleaned up). Another critical issue with the "map" command in dedicated servers has also been addressed so that server admins can now actually change the game to a specific map rather than being limited to just skipping maps. Finally, some crashes related to the engine have also been fixed, such as the one that was caused by the image generation system for some of your in-game icons.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.3.1932
notes.notes:
This update slightly increases the radius of M67 and RGD-5 grenades to provide more explosive damage for just a bit farther distances than before. It fixes a bug with the newly added armory commands from working for certain users in dedicated servers. We also fixed an issue in the HUD that prevented stats from displaying after you're killed that show how much damage you did to the player that killed you.

There's some debug information that we're now outputting to the console at the end of a match to allow us to diagnose an important issue that occasionally prevents MVPs from being selected for certain teams. We also corrected a problem with the new armory system causing player skins to leak between maps.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.2.1928
notes.notes:
This update adjusts some of the explosive calculations when trying to figure out if players are receiving damage from grenades. It may help in certain situations where a grenade felt as if it should have killed an enemy when it did not. This is due to the damage distances being adjusted in a previous update. After trying out these changes we plan to apply a small damage increase in the next update.

There's also a new "music" command that lets you set the volume of the in-game round start music and win music. This setting saves with your other audio settings and is synchronized via Steam Cloud across all your computers.

The console has also been updated with a list of in-game weapons that autocompletes when using the "primary" and "secondary" commands. These commands now have confirmation messages as well so you know if a valid weapon name was provided or not. Finally we'll include team detection in the next update so that only the available weapons on your current team will be listed.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.1.1924
notes.notes: This update fixes some critical issues with console commands crashing dedicated servers. It also adds a few temporary console commands such as "primary" and "secondary" to change your weapon in single-life game modes.

notes.title: Task Force 0.5.0.1921
notes.notes:
This update migrates the entire Task Force Alpha from Unreal Engine 4 to Unreal Engine 5. It brings a whole new set of possibilities for us as developers which we are still exploring and learning. The new engine will have significantly better graphics, such as a dynamic sky system with volumetric clouds and a dynamic weather system that includes rain, snow, ect. There’s also an all new character system which has realistic hair simulation along with detailed skin shaders and facial rigging. Again we are still in the process of experimenting with all this new technology so it will take some time before we get all our assets updated, but it’s an important first step into staying relevant by utilizing modern technology throughout the course of development. This also allows workshop mappers making custom maps to use some of the latest content on the Unreal Engine Marketplace for their maps since we were previously on a very old version of the engine which they no longer supported on the marketplace.

There’s an all new leaning system. Now instead of just curving your spine the character will actually step out and lean around the corner. It includes a detailed physics penetration system to ensure players cannot abuse the leaning by clipping their character or camera into any walls or other objects. The ground is also checked so players cannot lean out into the air when standing near ledges. Plus the new leaning system corrects an issue where players used to shake or jitter while you were spectating them. This was due to some networking conflicts in our animation system which has now been fixed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/a4e97077d55789488c482b954343e89e124797b8.gif[/img]

We’ve added new breach and escort game modes. The breach game mode is similar to the demolition game mode but only allows the breaching team to pick up the bomb. It supports breach in both directions so workshop mappers can setup custom maps that have either team as the breaching team depending on which bomb zones are available on the map. It also prevents the non-breaching team from triggering breach points, so only the breaching team can trigger breach points. The escort game mode uses VIPs instead of hostages. They start with the Special Forces in this game mode instead of the Terrorists. The Special Forces must extract 2 out of the 3 VIPs while keeping them alive. Conversely the Terrorists can win by eliminating all of the VIPs. We updated demolition mode as well to end early if everyone on the defusing team has died, so now you don’t have to sit around waiting for the bomb to explode. And finally all game modes have been updated with objective messages at the start of the round, along with some new mid-round messages. This includes when hostages are grabbed by the Special Forces in extraction mode or when the perimeter is breached in breach mode.

The third-person camera system has been overhauled to have smooth transitions. Now when crouching or proning the camera will no longer snap as it did before when looking up or down. It will smoothly blend between each position while still being quick and responsive. This can also be seen when viewing the “diamonds” on teammates which should now smoothly blend between their different positions when changing stances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/fa0167f1ee280dafd511da748f17e10b07e5ce6a.gif[/img]

There’s an all new jumping system which has a significantly lower jump height. Now players won’t feel floaty as if they’re jumping on the moon. This was due to the default functionality of the Unreal Engine which requires the physics object of all characters to be “standing” while in jump mode. This means even though you’re picking up your feet in the animation you see, the actual physics of the game never picked up your feet and you could never make it over even relatively low ledges and objects. In order to overcome this limitation many games have to utilize an extremely exaggerated jump height to allow players to make it over ledges and objects they would normally expect to be able to jump over. So we built a completely custom system within the Unreal Engine that properly shrinks the character while jumping to simulate the effect of picking your feet up when coming off the ground.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/e2bb3037c5efaac2a85c09accdc07f58c462fdf0.gif[/img]

This means you can now jump over any object you would normally expect to be able to jump over without actually requiring a huge jump height that makes you feel floaty. These new jump mechanics have also been completely integrated into the existing Unreal Engine movement system for networked multiplayer and feel significantly better than the vanilla jumping system that comes with the engine, which is what we were originally using.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/1c3082627428549079a665f1995478bc6faef862.gif[/img]

An all new stats and rankings system has been implemented. There is now a nicely polished round stats screen at the end of each round. It defaults to displaying 4v4 data unless there are more than 4 players on a team, in which case it shows 8v8 data instead. There’s also a stats summary screen at the end of each game which shows team totals and the top players on each team along with selecting MVPs for the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/44b0217ab178086fc79d2b8db8c23e079e0f2792.png[/img]

There are now live rank icons being fed via our website into the dedicated servers which update in real time. These ranks display on the round stats and game stats screens next to your name when playing on dedicated servers. Your live rank is also visible on Discord with a small rank icon (when you have game activity enabled in Discord). There are no ranks visible when playing in user-hosted lobbies and no stats are logged while playing in user-hosted lobbies. You can also view live global rankings and your own live player stats using the in-game overlay menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/55c3822976a04c17c536fc5480e068152dbce9fb.png[/img]

We’ve now set up proper “killer handoff” for certain equipment items such as breach points and the bomb in demolition modes. Previously these devices wouldn’t provide any killer information so it would say that the “world” killed someone with C-4. This also created an unintended glitch where players could kill the hostages with breach points yet it wouldn’t count against them. Now breaches along with the bomb in demolition modes will properly credit the killer that either triggered the breach or planted the bomb. There’s also individual bullet tracking for hits in the new stats system. This was critical for new weapons such as shotguns since you only fire one “shot” but can hit a player many times in many different hitboxes with that single shot. This would confuse the stats system and result in hit percentages that weren’t technically possible since there could potentially be more hits than shots. Now instead we log all hits on each individual hitbox but also store unique hits per shot in order to calculate accurate hit percentages in the new stats system.

The scoreboard is now more in parity with the official stats system. Previously if you killed a teammate after the round was over this was logged on the scoreboard. It counted against your score and your teammate received a death, which sometimes would create friction between players in games that would eventually lead to a bunch of teamkilling. This was a common misconception because no official stats are actually logged once the round is over, so everything happening afterwards doesn’t really matter. However we’ve now updated the scoreboard so that teamkills after the round is over don’t hurt your score or give a death to your teammate. Plus it doesn’t show a notification in the kill feed anymore either. This is also the case if you planted the bomb and it kills your teammates at the end of the round, it will not count against you. Most importantly you can still get kills on enemies after the round is over, these kills will count on the scoreboard, and your enemy’s death will count against them. And these kills on enemies will still show a notification in the kill feed after the round is over.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/8ce3462c25752adcfc296524f2a40d5511cecb48.png[/img]

We’ve added all new equipment such as M84 flashbangs which blind and deafen any players in their radius. There’s now incendiary grenades such as the AN-M14 and Molotov Cocktails along with PMN-1 mines and remotely detonated Claymores. We’ve revamped the M67 and M18 models. And we have various sounds for certain equipment that we didn’t take the time to implement before, such as the sound of smoke grenades bouncing or hissing. Finally the M67 has been replaced by the RGD-5 on the Terrorists side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/1a8a4b13ca331e24cd3a34864b12ff20c47748a7.gif[/img]

There’s all new bomb mechanics for demolition. You will now actually bend down and crouch to plant or defuse the bomb. This includes all new animations for taking off your backpack along with some sounds for arming or disarming the bomb and an ominous bomb beep while the timer is running. We also implemented various anti-glitch measures for demolition mode. This prevents players from causing the bomb to “fall off the map” and will instead teleport the bomb back to its previous pickup location.

There’s all new hostage mechanics for extraction. Previously hostages would always approach the location of the player they were following. This caused them to “bunch up” at the same time and created significant gameplay conflicts where they would get stuck in doorways and wouldn’t immediately run towards the extraction. Now they will instead create a “chain” effect where each hostage follows the most recent hostage you’ve grabbed. This prevents them from getting stuck in doorways or other small pathways since they now move in a more effective single file line.

This update includes an all new physics implementation. We’ve allowed players to shoot objects such as weapons or equipment and cause them to go flying. Any explosive forces will also cause objects on the ground to go flying in the air. This means your frag grenades can make smoke grenades or other equipment move to another location upon detonation, or cause the bomb to move to a new position (when the bomb is not planted). However we’ve limited the bomb to explosive forces only so you cannot shoot the bomb to make it slide away even if it’s just dropped on the ground.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/ff144c9d57548e48cb8f1af10dd36ad3f000c770.gif[/img]

We’ve implemented an all new ragdoll system. The characters should look a lot more natural when they ragdoll upon death whereas before they looked a bit stiff. We carefully tuned the interactions of various bones so that ragdolls are much more flexible than before while also feeling as if they have a more appropriate weight such that they don’t go flying like a feather due to explosive forces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/bca5cf4875384e1002dfefec7b926af25eac922d.gif[/img]

There are now primary weapon drops upon death. This means you can pick up the weapons of other players after they die. It’s similar to the functionality originally available in the shooting range but now includes a more proper physics implementation. That means grenades or other explosive devices will cause weapons on the ground to go flying. You can also shoot weapons on the ground to get them to slide away.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/0b356a8b9bef2b41a2298905142c2e93c526b990.gif[/img]

An all new armory has been created in the overlay menu system. We’ve removed the legacy armory that was part of the HUD and included an updated armory that showcases your current character skin along with a preview of your current weapon selection. It allows you to cycle through weapon types and select equipment such as frag grenades, smoke grenades, flashbangs, incendiary grenades, or mines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/927c518481c3f036cb0259179c7220920d88aac4.png[/img]

The entire settings system has been overhauled. We originally used Unreal Engine INI files to store user settings which were extremely limiting. It also exposed a lot of dangerous functionality that allowed players to disable certain elements of the game such as grass or foliage by adjusting settings they weren’t supposed to have access to. Now we’re using a completely custom system instead. It uses JSON files that are very easy to edit and are now also synchronized across all your computers using Steam Cloud Sync. This means if you change your bindings on one computer they’ll be there on a different computer when you login to Steam. Most importantly these new files only contain the specific settings we’ve included which prevents players from altering aspects of the engine that weren’t intended to be changed. Therefore we’ve completely locked out Unreal Engine INI functionality and all user settings must be implemented via these custom JSON files.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/00ad14adc44297fe3733bea7250e81c3daac92eb.png[/img]

There’s an all new bindings system which is much more dynamic than before. It organizes bindings into “binding groups” which allows you to setup various configurations for different parts of the game which may share the same keys. A good example of this are bindings you may have for your character vs bindings you may have for drivable vehicles. These configurations can now use the same keys without conflicting with each other. This is also great news for QWE players as you can now rebind your WASD keys. And finally we fixed an issue that prevented players from binding jump to their scroll wheel, which was a known bug.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/61af6ae5cff200223d4229c565994ad4be69f624.png[/img]

We’ve overhauled the entire settings menu. It has also been created in the overlay menu system with the new armory. It provides various options for graphics, sound, and key bindings. There’s even some new settings available such as selecting a specific output device for your audio output or a specific input device for your microphone input. These options weren’t previously available but now we actually provide a drop-down list of available audio output and input devices similar to how Discord does. It also changes these devices dynamically in real time without requiring you to restart the game. This should prevent any issues with players having problems where their microphone isn’t working since everything is now easily accessible and configurable. We’ve even upgraded the audio quality of the in-game voice comms so players should sound a lot better than before.

The new bindings system has also been completely integrated with the player notifications system. This means whenever you have the ability to interact with an object it will actually say “Press <KEY> to…” with a key icon rather than just a generic message. It even automatically toggles between keyboard and controller users in real time to display the proper keybinding. There’s also new player notifications for reloading when your mag is low and “out of ammo” messages when you’re out of ammo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/51c0239e60811f44dcff4c34fc974f9725828373.gif[/img]

We implemented a new cinematic camera system to complement the new round stats and game MVP screens. There will now be a random camera angle chosen between each round and at the end of the game which will be the background for the new stats screens. It is synchronized on the server so every player is looking at the same camera between rounds and at the end of the game. This means workshop mappers can now place cameras around their maps to set up different viewpoints that will be randomly selected for this effect. It also spawns your initial spectator camera in one of these camera locations when first joining a game rather than randomly putting you under the map or at some weird location that makes the competitive experience feel unpolished.

There’s also been many spectator bugs that were fixed up. Previously when switching from a player’s camera perspective to freecam mode it would pop you into the center of the player and made the spectating experience feel rather lackluster. Now you will properly detach from the locked camera at the exact location so it feels like a smooth camera transition. This effect is also used when players die so that the camera transition is smooth when it unlocks upon death. The “next player” and “previous player” spectate buttons (left/right click) have been updated for freecam as well since they didn’t make sense. Now if you press either of these buttons in freecam it will select the player you are pointing your camera at that is closest to you. It will not select any players behind your camera. This makes the competitive spectator experience much smoother in freecam mode as you can now instantly attach and detach from players as you are flying around in a way that feels very natural and effective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/261a4e91179eb16a0bc1adcdccc988b67e59080f.gif[/img]

There’s some very significant optimizations across the entire game in this update. We’ve rebuilt the bullet impacts system and character footsteps system so that they no longer spam the game world. This also means that workshop map developers will have bullet holes and footprints properly disappear on meshes that they may dynamically show or hide since everything is actually attached now and a subcomponent of the object it’s hitting. We also “primed” all audio for our weapons and VFX to prevent them from delayed loading. This means that shooting your weapon or triggering an explosion should feel a bit “snappier” since it’s no longer loading content as it happens but rather preloading this content as it should.

This update reconfigures many of the networking settings of the Unreal Engine in order to provide an improved multiplayer experience than what we had previously. We’ve updated the way some important gameplay information is synchronized over the network to make it smoother when spectating other players and following their camera movements. The bomb mechanics have also been completely overhauled in order to ensure everything works in proper lock step when it comes to the timing of defusing vs the end of the round or planting/defusing vs when a player is actually killed. There’s now network synchronization as well that fixes an issue where multiple players could be defusing the bomb at the same time. This is all integrated with the action notification system so it doesn’t suggest that you can perform these actions if they aren’t available, even when it comes to network-controlled actions such as defusing or taking control of hostages.

We implemented an all new anti-cheat system. It does some really incredible cutting edge stuff but we’re not going to elaborate anymore on this for obvious reasons. Just know that we take cheating very seriously and will do whatever we can to prevent it.

We’ve now properly organized your game files into various groups in order to streamline updates via Steam. This means certain game content that doesn’t change frequently will be grouped together on your install drive to minimize the “disk” portion of your Steam updates, including large files such as textures and meshes. However other content that does change frequently will be grouped together into small files that make your Steam updates minimize the amount of disk overwriting required. Long story short, whenever you update your game on Steam it should be quick and efficient rather than sitting there waiting for almost all of your game content to be overridden even if the update had a download size that was only a fraction of how much content it has to rewrite on your install drive.

We’ve created an automatic world analysis system which dynamically calculates the bottom of the map. This will prevent players from “falling off the map” when it’s not properly sealed off, which is a common occurrence on workshop maps. Instead an automatic Kill-Z will be calculated and enforced on your map to prevent players from falling indefinitely until the round timer expires.

The console has been significantly updated with cleaner output and improved highlighting of commands. It has all new autocomplete functionality which makes learning commands much easier too. For instance when you type the map command it will now list the names of all the maps in the game along with any custom workshop maps you’ve subscribed to. This data updates in real time as well when you subscribe to new maps or unsubscribe from existing maps. Then after putting the map name it will list all the available game modes for that map including workshop integration so it only lists the game modes that the workshop mapper specified in their item tags. Similarly when using the bind command it will list all the available key names that the game supports. Then after putting the key name it shows all the possible bindings in the game. You can also now use your up/down arrow keys to cycle through previous commands as you would in other consoles, which makes it much easier to quickly fix a command that you might have typed wrong. There’s some great performance enhancements as well such as “batched messages” which now prevents the console from getting clogged up due to message spam. For instance when uploading a custom map there’s a lot of console output from the cooker as it goes through all your assets. This would previously cause the console to get extremely laggy whereas now the console will remain quick and snappy during the entire process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/e663ff84dfd8d43e577e23a111f26c435852afcc.gif[/img]

We now have missing asset detection rerouted to your console during map load. That means if you’re using some assets on your custom map that are no longer in the game you will see red error messages in your console telling you which assets are missing from your map. It also tells you which actors or blueprints include the reference so you know where to go to fix the problem.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/cfa3766f24b18a0980f286b3724b7fe0df1e6e6b.png[/img]

This migration to Unreal Engine 5 includes some really big updates for workshop mappers. We now provide a custom build of the Unreal Editor via our GitHub repository instead of downloading a vanilla editor in the Epic Games Launcher (an Epic Games account is still required to access GitHub). There’s a ton of customizations in this editor build along with some various plugins which are included with the game. This means you can work with the cooked plugin of our sky system, setup dynamic times of day, dynamic weather, ect. And you won’t have to include any of these assets in your map because it will already be part of the in-game download. You can also access the cooked version of our volumetric landscape plugin to carve out the ground for more intuitive landscape development. It’s significantly better than having to carve “holes” using the default landscape system that comes with the engine. We’ve included a simple snapping plugin as well which makes it so much easier to snap meshes together or change the rotation origin of meshes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/daccbee2d76866ac8cfefda32b1a425b3dfcfc57.png[/img]

There’s also a ton of documentation compared to a year ago which should make it a lot easier to get into custom map development now that there’s very detailed step by step instructions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/ee0e7f60424d1f26926915b11c95e7d7bd354e27.png[/img]

The most important feature though of this new workshop system is the ability to extract cooked in-game content directly from your game installation directory. We have a new wizard that displays when you launch this custom engine build which allows you to create a project using various templates based on the type of map you want to make. Once you’ve made a project there’s an option to extract game content from your Task Force installation directory so you can use textures, materials, and meshes that are part of the in-game content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/8723565ac56333176169be1467700d1a7616cd06.png[/img]

This also significantly reduces the upload/download size of your custom map because none of this content needs to be included since it’s part of the official game. It makes things a lot easier for workshop mappers too because buying content on the Unreal Engine Marketplace requires you to prep that content for the game with proper physics and collision. However if a workshop mapper is using cooked content directly from the official game all this content is already good to go. You just grab whatever you want and start using it immediately. So being able to access and use in-game content is a huge step forward for workshop mappers compared to our previous workshop system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/209db3527cc4452d5f23f41c0f05166f8837d488.png[/img]

We’ve added “development” footprints and bullet holes on surfaces that do not have a physics type configured. This is important for workshop mappers in case they forget to set the physics on their materials. Previously you would just run around silent until you realized you had no footstep sounds and then would wonder why. It’s also not as apparent for walls because there was always a default bullet hole, but without proper physics it never had a particle effect or sound. So now we display these default footprints and bullet holes on surfaces without any physics type which makes it much more obvious for workshop mappers that they need to fix something on their maps. If you happen to see any checkerboard footprints or bullet holes now you know why and can report the issue with the proper surface marked accordingly in your screenshots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30694736/226722796bd5360e86ae2341830eb688b793eb46.gif[/img]

Here’s our roadmap for what’s next…

0.6.0 / 0.7.0 / 0.8.0 / 0.9.0

[list]
[*]All new first person gameplay with custom first person animations, aim down sights, and a fully animated body when looking down at the ground
[*]Weapon attachments such as sights, scopes, suppressors, muzzle brakes, lasers, flashlights, ect.
[*]Add new weapons such as the M60, M249, G36, P90, HK416, M82, M40, SVD, Desert Eagle, Makarov, MP40, a few shotguns, and more
[*]Fully integrated competitive system with automatic server creation for scheduled matches, detailed stats logging and immediate loss reporting
[*]Finalized armory with complete character customization
[*]All new ballistics system with real world material penetration and ricochet simulation along with bullet drop and bullet time for long distance shots in a hybrid hitscan / bullet time system
[*]Steam achievements and unlockable skins (cosmetic only)
[*]TaskForceTV 2.0
[/list]
